sentences.text: [serious] Forty, and earning eight thousand a month? Fidelity says you should have two hundred and eighty-eight thousand saved.
Thirty: ninety-six thousand. Fifty: five seventy-six. Sixty-seven: nine hundred and sixty thousand. Where are you?

visual.title: Where are you? · $8K/mo salary
visual.source: Fidelity guideline: 1x salary by 30, 3x by 40, 6x by 50, 8x by 60, 10x by 67

sentences.text: [reassuring] Behind? The usual advice is spend less. But that won't work unless the saving happens first.
Fidelity's guideline assumes you save fifteen percent of your income every year, from age twenty-five, match included.

visual.source: Includes any employer match. A guideline, not a rule.

sentences.text: On eight thousand a month, that's twelve hundred. And it only happens if it leaves on payday, before anything else.
Then what's left is yours to spend, with a daily number that adjusts when you overspend.
[warm] So find your age, then make payday the day you save. Save first. Then spend what's safe. Try it at Divvyup dot com.
